steps.description:
The adapters component lives under `src/adapters`.  In this tour we focus on the four files that establish the basic adapter vocabulary:

- `ITokenAdapter.sol` – the canonical interface all token-level adapters must satisfy.
- `EulerUSDCAdapter.sol` – a concrete implementation for Euler’s interest-bearing USDC token.
- `ETHUSDConverter.sol` – a small library that converts between ETH and USD amounts using a Chainlink price feed.
- `ETHUSDPriceFeedAdapter.sol` – an on-chain wrapper that exposes the converter behind a simple price-feed interface.

ITokenAdapter defines the four read-only functions every adapter must expose.  Notice that the interface contains no state – only these view functions which external contracts, such as the vaults, can call to discover adapter details or fetch a price.

EulerUSDCAdapter is an example of an adapter that fulfils the interface.  Lines 11-15 declare:  
- `version` – a human-readable constant so clients can detect breaking changes.  
- `token` & `underlyingToken` – `immutable` addresses recorded once in the constructor (lines 17-19).  These parameters tell external contracts which yield token is handled and what the underlying asset is.

ETHUSDConverter is a Solidity `library` (line 6).  The header comment and custom errors (lines 7-10) announce its purpose: safe conversion between ETH values and their USD representation, relying on a Chainlink price feed passed in by callers.

ETHUSDPriceFeedAdapter wraps the converter into a contract.  Lines 8-24 declare the `IPriceFeedAdapter` interface it implements.  Lines 27-41 show the adapter’s own state: the chosen price-feed address, an acceptable staleness window, and the decimals of the underlying token – all supplied through the constructor so the same code can be deployed to different chains or tokens.

Together these four files illustrate the adapter pattern:  
1. A thin, immutable contract (`EulerUSDCAdapter`) or library wrapper (`ETHUSDPriceFeedAdapter`) declares what it adapts via constructor arguments.  
2. Callers interact only through small view functions defined in an interface (`ITokenAdapter` or `IPriceFeedAdapter`).  
3. Auxiliary maths (`ETHUSDConverter`) stays separate, ensuring each adapter remains focused on translating a single asset or price feed.
